audit.limitation: A literal-phrase guard. It catches the wordings the owner named and cannot detect an overstatement phrased in words nobody listed. Terminology consistency beyond these phrases is documentation_only.

terms.does_not_mean: That a measured proportion of a known behaviour space has been exercised. No such space is enumerated, so no proportion exists.

terms.means: A counted set of offline scenarios, each asserting one governance property by driving the real modules and observing the real refusal. Reported as a count, never as a percentage.
terms.does_not_mean: That the scenarios bound what an agent can do.

terms.means: A local model produced output, a documented rubric scored it, and the run is recorded with model, prompt and seed. Establishes what one model did on one host at one moment.
terms.does_not_mean: That the model will behave the same way again, that a different model would behave this way, or that the behaviour is enforced.
Anything specific. It was used for both deterministic refusal scenarios and model-scored behaviour, which are different claims.
terms.replacement: governance refusal scenario (deterministic) or behaviour evaluation (model evaluated)

terms.means: A scripted mission executed end to end with no model, no network and no provider. Every value is authored in the script.
terms.does_not_mean: That an agent's reasoning was reproduced. Nothing is inferred; the script asserts the governance path, not the thinking.

terms.means: An owner-reviewed statement about one commit, naming one verdict token, its evidence and its limitations.
terms.does_not_mean: Fitness for production, external audit, or any claim about a model.

terms.means: The code path cannot proceed: an exception is raised or a non-zero exit is returned. Always written with its tier attached.
terms.does_not_mean: That an instruction in a prompt was obeyed. Prompt text is never enforcement; it is advisory_only.

terms.means: Scripted sequencing of participants and stages by the runner. The sequence is fixed in code and takes no model input.
terms.does_not_mean: That an agent decides what happens next. Where the *workflow* refuses to advance, the correct phrase is orchestration-checked.
Anything this system does. Every execution is operator-initiated, every authority flag is false by default, and no path merges, pushes or deploys.

terms.means: Reserved for the SaathiOS product runtime — the agents that serve users at request time — or for the adverb sense, at execution time.
terms.does_not_mean: Any component of this package. The execution engine here is the deterministic runner; naming it a runtime would collide with saathi/platform/mission_runtime/.

terms.means: A gate record naming an approver who is not the subject author, bound to evidence artifact ids. Refused otherwise.
terms.does_not_mean: Owner approval. That is a distinct, owner-only gate that no agent and no automation can satisfy.

terms.means: A saathi.safety.SafetyLevel ceiling declared in a role contract and checked when the registry loads.
terms.does_not_mean: A capability granted to a running process. A contract describes what a role may ask for, not what the operating system permits.
